paras: The Hutchinson near-lynching was a racial confrontation in Hutchinson, Kansas, reported in April 1903, in which a Black man who stepped on a white man's foot was attacked and, according to a Wichita paper, 'nearly' lynched. No one was reported killed, and the trouble ended when the white man left. The episode is known only from two jesting items in Kansas state-news columns, one of which likened it to the Joplin riot.

Neither report gives a date for the incident, names the men involved, or says where in Hutchinson it took place. According to the Wichita Daily Eagle, a 'colored man' had 'tramped on a white man's toes'; the Topeka State Journal said he trod on the white man's 'corns'. The Eagle reported that the Black man was then 'jumped onto' and that 'there was nearly a lynching', without saying who attacked him or how many took part.

In response, the Eagle said, the man 'rounded up his friends'. The same item said that 'the exit of the white man was all that averted calling out the state troops', which suggests the standoff ended when he left.
No report of arrests, charges, or any official inquiry appears in the coverage, and the troops were not called out.

Both reports appeared on 24 April 1903 as brief items in humorous roundups of Kansas news. The Eagle ran its two sentences in 'Along the Kansas Nile' between quips about Arbor Day and an elopement reported from Wellington, in a tone that neither condemned nor approved the threatened lynching. The State Journal's 'Jayhawker Jots' gave it a single line, placed beside items on sunbonnet socials and carpet-sewing bees, saying the incident 'almost started a race war equal to the Joplin riot.'
Neither paper treated the episode as news in its own right, and no follow-up, wire report, or Black-press account of it was found.

accounts.label: Wichita Daily Eagle column
accounts.gist: A colored man stepped on a white man's toes and there was 'nearly a lynching'; after being jumped on he rounded up his friends, and only the white man's departure averted calling out the state troops.

accounts.label: Topeka State Journal column
accounts.gist: A colored man treading on a white man's corns at Hutchinson almost started a race war comparable to the Joplin riot.
